competitors.name: Prighter
competitors.what_they_do: Sells EU GDPR, UK GDPR, Swiss FADP, Turkiye KVKK, DSA, Data Act and AI Act GPAI representative services, plus NIS2 and e-Evidence support. Bundling is already a product: its pricing page offers 'up to 40%' off for combining representative services, at 10% per extra product. Public prices are about EUR 35-396 per month per service, billed annually. It has a 'Privacy Rights Manager' tool in development and an 'Incident Manager' coming soon, and ISO 27001:2022 certification. Customers named on its homepage include DuckDuckGo, Vevo and Elementor. This is the closest match to the idea.
competitors.scale_or_funding: Funding and client count not disclosed. Crunchbase returned 403, so I could not check it. Homepage: https://prighter.com

competitors.name: EDPO (European Data Protection Office)
competitors.what_they_do: Brussels-headquartered provider of GDPR (EU/EEA), UK GDPR, Swiss FADP, Monaco, AI Act, NIS2, Data Governance Act and Data Act representative services, with an affiliate (EDSR) covering e-Evidence, DSA and TCO. Flat fees are priced by employee count and data volume, and include unlimited data-subject requests, translations and breach-notification support. It offers AI Act authorised-representative service to GPAI and high-risk providers, keeps documentation for 10 years, is ISO 27001 certified, and says it carries extensive insurance. Offices in Brussels, London and Geneva, with satellite offices in Paris, Dublin, Madrid, Berlin, Amsterdam, Sofia and Stockholm.
competitors.scale_or_funding: 'Hundreds of companies'; client testimonials include Shell. Funding not disclosed. AI Act page: https://edpo.com/ai-act-representative/

competitors.name: DataRep
competitors.what_they_do: Representative services under EU GDPR, UK GDPR, Swiss FADP, DSA, NIS and NIS2, TCO, DGA, EU AI Act and EU Data Act. It offers one package with 'no separate pricing for different regulation types', a next-working-day acknowledgment SLA, unlimited communications, and contact points in 29 EU/EEA states. Its AI Act and Data Act pages say 'we are finalising our service', so those two offerings are not yet live.
competitors.scale_or_funding: Clients in 25+ countries; claims its clients process over 350 million data subjects. Prices start at EUR 150 per year, with renewal discounts of up to 50%. Funding not disclosed.

competitors.name: VeraSafe
competitors.what_they_do: Long-standing US/Czech provider of GDPR and UK GDPR representative and privacy services. I could not verify its current AI Act, Data Act or bundle offering because the site returned 403 to every fetch. Treat it as an established Art. 27 incumbent and a likely acquirer or copier.

competitors.name: Obelis Group
competitors.what_they_do: Product-side authorised representative and responsible person, founded in 1988. It covers medical devices and IVDs, cosmetics, GPSR general products, food supplements, toys, machinery, batteries, ATEX, EMC and more, in the EU, UK, Switzerland, Canada, US and Turkiye. It has in-house regulatory affairs teams and does real liability-bearing representation. Its site does not mention GDPR, AI Act, Data Act or CRA, so it is adjacent today but would be the most natural incumbent to add those.
competitors.scale_or_funding: Over 7,000 manufacturers from 90+ countries, per its site. Private and unfunded as far as I found.

white_space:
Verdict basis: the digital-regulation half of the idea (GDPR Art. 27 + AI Act + Data Act + NIS2 + DSA) is already served by at least three established providers, each with a multi-regulation catalog. Prighter has a live bundle discount and EDPO has flat all-inclusive packages. Four things remain unserved or weakly served.

1. Hardware and connected-product makers. The privacy and digital reps (Prighter, EDPO, DataRep) do not appear to offer GPSR, CRA or sector product-safety representation, and the product-side rep (Obelis) does not appear to offer GDPR, AI Act, Data Act or CRA. Nobody I found sells both halves. The buyer is a non-EU IoT, consumer-electronics or industrial-AI company that needs GPSR responsible person, Data Act representative, GDPR Art. 27, CRA and AI Act Art. 22 at once. This is the only wedge that survives.

2. Genuinely substantive, liability-bearing representation. AI Act Art. 22 obliges the rep to verify the declaration of conformity and technical documentation, hold documents for 10 years and terminate the mandate if the provider breaches. Art. 54 gives the GPAI rep a similar duty over Annex XI documentation. Vendors such as EDPO explicitly disclaim internal compliance and act as a liaison. A rep that actually reviews the technical file (an 'AI Act notified-body-lite' role) is a different, higher-priced product that I did not find anyone offering at scale.

3. Execution gaps. DataRep's AI Act and Data Act pages still say 'finalising our service', and none of the vendors publish a shared cross-regulation register of representations, SLA-backed triage, or unified invoicing beyond a discount.

4. Timing. CRA vulnerability and incident reporting applies from 11 Sep 2026 (EC page: https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/cyber-resilience-act), with main obligations from 11 Dec 2027. The CRA authorised representative is optional and narrow, so it is a weak demand driver.

Roll-up thesis weaknesses. (a) Market price points are far below the idea's EUR 3-15k per bundle: about EUR 420-4,750 per year per service at Prighter, and from EUR 150 at DataRep, with 40% bundle discounts. (b) The AI Act rep TAM is small: only non-EU GPAI providers and non-EU high-risk providers, and open-source GPAI is exempt under Art. 54(6) unless it poses systemic risk. (c) GDPR Art. 27 representation is largely a commodity postbox, so 'someone who can be sued' commands little premium in that segment. (d) I found no evidence of small rep shops being for sale at 1-2x revenue, and Prighter, EDPO and DataRep are natural competing acquirers.
evidence_of_demand:
Demand is real, but mostly statutory and inferred rather than direct customer complaints. Web search budget ran out after the first attempts, so I found no forum threads, RFPs or Product Hunt or YC data. Findings:

1. Legal mandates. AI Act Art. 22 (high-risk providers outside the EU must appoint a Union-established authorised representative): https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/article/22/. Art. 54 (third-country GPAI providers must appoint one, with a 10-year Annex XI documentation duty and an open-source exemption unless the model has systemic risk): https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/article/54/. CRA reporting obligations from 11 Sep 2026 and main obligations from 11 Dec 2027: https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/cyber-resilience-act.

2. A paid market exists and is already segmenting by regulation. Prighter publishes per-regulation prices and bundle discounts: https://prighter.com/pricing. EDPO sells an AI Act representative service to GPAI and high-risk providers: https://edpo.com/ai-act-representative/. DataRep claims clients in 25+ countries: https://www.datarep.com. Obelis claims over 7,000 manufacturers on the product side: https://www.obelis.net.

3. Recognizable customers (DuckDuckGo, Vevo, Elementor at Prighter; Shell at EDPO) show the buyer set includes mid-size and large non-EU firms.

4. Not verified: a Dutch DPA fine on Locatefamily.com for failing to designate an Art. 27 representative, recalled from memory. The EDPB page fetch did not confirm it.

Missing: any evidence that buyers want one bundle for multiple representative obligations, or will pay EUR 3-15k. Prighter's price list suggests they pay far less for the digital regulations. The claimed 70-80% renewal rate and 1-2x revenue acquisition multiples are unsupported.
kill_reason: n/a. As written (a roll-up selling a bundle of digital-regulation representatives) the idea is crowded: Prighter, EDPO and DataRep already sell multi-regulation representation, and Prighter already sells the bundle discount. It is not killed because a specific wedge remains open: bridging privacy and digital representatives with product-safety and CRA representatives for hardware and connected-product makers, using a substantive AI Act and Data Act rep. Confidence is moderate-to-low, because web search was exhausted early, VeraSafe and Crunchbase were blocked, and no acquisition-market data was found. Treat this as a conditional pass that needs a pivot.
sharper_angle: Drop the generic 'one contract for every rep' roll-up. Sell a single EU Compliance Presence for non-EU hardware, IoT and industrial-AI makers ($5M-$200M revenue), covering GPSR or sector responsible-person duties, Data Act legal representative, GDPR Art. 27, AI Act Art. 22 authorised representative and optional CRA support, backed by a conformity-file reviewer. Differentiate on real technical-file verification and a shared register of representations with a shared evidence vault, not on a postbox. Price it at a premium (about EUR 8-25k per year) because the rep verifies documents and can terminate the mandate. Buy or partner with one product-side rep shop (Obelis-type) and one digital rep shop (Prighter/EDPO/DataRep-type) rather than three privacy postbox shops. Skip GDPR-only reps, which are priced from EUR 150-4,750 per year. Before committing, validate three things the research could not: (1) how many non-EU high-risk AI and connected-hardware firms are actually buying multiple reps, (2) what the product-side reps charge for CRA and AI Act, and (3) whether professional-indemnity insurers will underwrite the liability at a viable premium.
